title: The context-monitor hooks written into every consumer settings.json use an invalid schema and have never fired
description:
**Found while reviewing TASK-209, escalated as a research question, and now confirmed against the official Claude Code documentation and against this repo's own code.**

**The defect.** `buildContextMonitorEntries` (`src/claude-settings.js`) produces hook entries in a **flat** shape — `command` sitting directly on the array element, with **no inner `hooks` array**. Verified by executing it:

```
stopHook          -> { "type": "command", "command": "node \"...\\stop-hook.mjs\"" }
sessionStartHook  -> { "type": "command", "matcher": "clear|compact", "command": "node \"...\\session-start.mjs\"" }
```

`writeClaudeSettings` merges those straight into the consumer project's `.claude/settings.json`.

**That shape is a schema error.** The official hooks reference requires the nested form and states it explicitly: *"Hooks array is required: You cannot place a handler directly on the matcher group. Handlers must nest inside the `hooks` array."* The canonical shape is:

```json
{ "hooks": { "SessionStart": [ { "matcher": "...", "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "..." } ] } ] } }
```

**The plugin's own `hooks/hooks.json` already uses the correct nested shape** — so the two files disagree with each other, and only the plugin-side one is valid. The docs confirm both files share one schema (*"Copy the `hooks` object from your `.claude/settings.json`... since the format is the same"*), so there is no separate project-level dialect that would excuse the flat form.

**Consequence.** The context-monitor `Stop` and `SessionStart` hooks written into consumer projects have **most likely never executed**, since TASK-008/TASK-009 (June 2026). Everything that depends on them — context auto-flush, the HANDOFF.md snapshot on compact/clear — has been inert in every consumer install. The statusline is unaffected: `statusLine.command` is a different settings key with a different shape and is genuinely honoured.

**It fails silently.** Per the docs, an invalid entry is rejected or stripped with no warning unless the user runs `claude doctor` or `/hooks`. Nothing in the framework checks. This is why it went six weeks unnoticed and why it was misattributed to stale paths.

**Relationship to TASK-209 — read this before starting.** TASK-209 was raised from a human report of "the plugin address is hardcoded to an old version and stops being found after an update." Stale paths are real and `context-monitor/repin.mjs` does repair them, but the reviewer proved `repin.mjs` is **also blind to the nested shape** (it only walks `hooks[event][i].command`). So the two defects interlock: the entries are written in a shape that never fires, and the repair walks only that same never-firing shape. **Fixing the schema without fixing `repin.mjs`'s traversal would leave freshly-valid entries un-repairable on the next update, and fixing the traversal without the schema would repair entries that still never fire.** Coordinate with TASK-209 rather than racing it.

**Do not assume the fix is only a shape change.** Any project initialized before this ticket carries invalid entries on disk. A corrected writer helps new projects; existing ones need migration, and `--apply-settings` will not do it — its `hasStopHook`/`hasSessionStartHook` presence checks match the *stale/invalid* entry and skip the append (verified empirically during the TASK-209 review: it printed `already up-to-date (no write needed)` against a fully stale file).

**Verify the premise yourself before building.** This is a documentation-derived conclusion about another product's behaviour. Confirm empirically — write both shapes into a real project settings file, run `/hooks` and `claude doctor`, and record what each reports. If the flat shape turns out to be honoured after all, say so plainly and close this as invalid; that outcome is just as valuable and far cheaper than a wrong migration.
acceptance_criteria: The premise is verified empirically rather than inherited from documentation: both hook shapes are written into a real project settings file and the actual behaviour is recorded - whether each appears in /hooks, whether claude doctor reports a validation error, and whether the hook executes. State the evidence plainly, and if the flat shape is honoured after all, close this ticket as invalid rather than building on a wrong premise.

A failing spec first reproduces the defect at the level the fix will address - buildContextMonitorEntries emits a shape that does not match the documented nested schema. Capture the red-run output verbatim.

Hook entries written into a consumer .claude/settings.json use the documented nested shape, matching what the plugin's own hooks/hooks.json already uses, with matcher handled correctly per event (SessionStart supports it; Stop does not).

Projects initialized before this fix are migrated, not just newly-created ones. --apply-settings does not currently repair them because its presence checks match the invalid entry and skip the append - state what mechanism performs the migration and how a user who reads nothing gets it.

The migration is idempotent and never clobbers unrelated user content: a spec must prove an unrelated pre-existing hook and an unrelated pre-existing setting survive untouched, and that running it twice changes nothing the second time.

Coordinated with TASK-209's repin.mjs traversal so the two fixes compose: entries end up in a shape that both fires AND can be re-pointed when the plugin updates. State explicitly how the two interact.
A sensor pins the emitted shape against the documented schema so a future edit cannot silently regress to a non-firing form. Prove it non-vacuous by showing it red on the flat shape.
npm run test:all is green; dist rebuilt and committed if bundled source changes, with dist-parity passing.

comments.author: reviewer
comments.body:
**APPROVE** — final verdict across three rounds. FULL depth, tier `tdd`, priority critical. **0 HIGH / 0 MEDIUM / 0 LOW outstanding.**

Commits `49a3efb` → `d7e744c` → `16dfca3` → `a65040c`.

**Gate, reproduced exactly on a clean source tree:** `test:since -- 16dfca3~1` 5 files / 46 passed ⬛ `npm test` 94 files / 1248 passed | 2 skipped ⬛ **`test:all` 199 passed | 1 skipped (200 files), 2305 passed | 4 skipped, 0 failed** ⬛ `dist-parity` 2/2 green ⬛ `check:calibration` clean ⬛ `git status --porcelain` on source dirs empty.

**On dist — verified mechanically, not by rule.** `dist-parity` rebuilds all bundles with the same esbuild config into a temp dir and byte-compares against committed `dist/`. Green. That is the proof the comment-only edits produced byte-identical output; the comment-position heuristic did not have to be trusted.

## AC1 — the premise, reproduced independently

`claude doctor` (v2.1.223) run by the reviewer against two scratch fixtures:

```
flat:   Invalid settings
        hooks.Stop.0.hooks: Expected array, but received undefined
        hooks.SessionStart.0.hooks: Expected array, but received undefined
nested: No installation issues found.
```

Critically, the nested run used **the actual bytes** `mergeContextMonitorSettings({}, buildContextMonitorEntries(...))` emits — including `Stop` with no `matcher` key at all — not merely "a nested shape." The un-observed *firing* is a narrow residual: a hard schema rejection cannot have a code path to execution, and the TASK-209 reviewer independently watched the shipped 0.18.0 `repin.mjs` repair only `statusLine`. Premise adequately established.

**Red run replayed** against `a91e216:src/claude-settings.js`: exactly 4 load-bearing shape failures, with the `matcher` assertion correctly **passing** pre-fix. The developer's self-classification was accurate and did not inflate the count.

## HIGH-1 — race guard now genuinely exercised

The injectable `readSettings` seam defaults to the real `readFileSync`; `main()` passes no third argument; `existsSync` and the atomic write/rename/unlink path are untouched. The reviewer probed the branch directly:

```
race(diff 2nd) -> skipped-race
race(same 2nd) -> migrated
```

The branch is decided by the comparison, not the injection mechanics. The spec is stronger than the minimum in two ways: `expect(callCount).toBe(2)` fails if a future edit drops the pre-write re-read, and the final assertion reads the **real on-disk file** and requires byte-identity to the concurrent writer's content — so a write leaking past the guard is caught on disk, not merely in the return value.

## HIGH-2 — doc-lock is strict where it matters, and found a second defect

The reviewer extracted the marked block itself, diffed it against live output, and fed it synthetic drift:

```
doc Stop[0] == stopHook            : true
DRIFT unquoted command    -> caught: true
DRIFT Stop gains matcher  -> caught: true
DRIFT wrong filename      -> caught: true
DRIFT SS loses matcher    -> caught: true
SEPARATOR-only difference -> caught: false   (intentionally tolerated)
```

The normalization rewrites `\` → `/` in **string leaf values only**, applied to both sides, so quoting, the `node ` prefix, filenames and `matcher` presence are all compared exactly. Normalizing leaves rather than `JSON.stringify` + global replace was the right call — the latter would have mangled JSON's own `\"` escapes and silently defeated the quoting check.

**That the lock found the missing `node "<path>"` quoting while being built is the strongest evidence for it.** That defect had been in the doc since TASK-008 and neither reviewer nor developer caught it by reading.

## LOW-5 — one schema, one validator

`collectFormatViolations` extraction confirmed a byte-for-byte pure move. `plugin-hooks-format.spec.js` retains **both** non-vacuity tests and still runs 8. Four checks now share one validator.

## MEDIUM-1 — all six outcomes now reachable, distinguishable and covered

Five were verified by direct exercise; `write-failed` could not be forced on win32 (`chmod 0o500` on a directory is a no-op there), which is exactly why it went untested. The final round closed it **both halves** via an injectable `writeSettings` seam mirroring the existing read seam: the message assertion, and the real return path driven by a throwing writer with the on-disk file confirmed untouched.

Quiet outcomes are quiet by an explicit `return null`, asserted — **quiet by decision, not by omission**. No seventh indistinguishable case was introduced.

## Final round

Both items taken. The doc-lock asymmetry became a full comparison (`entries.statusLine` rather than a two-field projection), still green — confirming no extra fields today and making the lock symmetric across all three compared objects.

**LOW-1 / LOW-2 deferrals agreed on the merits:** first-match-only migration is unreachable through our own writer, and filename-substring ownership only ever replaces a *flat* entry, which is already schema-invalid and non-firing — nothing working can be destroyed. Consistent with `repin.mjs`'s precedent.

**`d7e744c` cleared of expectation-laundering:** every changed assertion moved from `h.command` to `h.hooks[].command`, strictly *stronger*, and the commit *added* a constraint. No expected value was loosened.

**Verdict: APPROVE.** Nothing remains open.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
**CLOSED on a green independent review after two fix rounds.** Review depth **FULL** throughout; rubric inputs: 1021 changed lines, packaging/dist (`dist/init.cjs`), a **new plugin-level `SessionStart` hook that runs in every consumer project**, and a mutation path over users' `.claude/settings.json`. Any one forces FULL.

Commits `49a3efb` → `d7e744c` → `16dfca3` → `a65040c`. Tier `tdd`, priority critical.

## What this actually was

`buildContextMonitorEntries` emitted a **flat** hook entry — `command` directly on the array element — where the documented schema requires **nested**. `claude doctor` rejects the flat form outright:

```
hooks.Stop.0.hooks: Expected array, but received undefined
hooks.SessionStart.0.hooks: Expected array, but received undefined
```

So the context-monitor `Stop` and `SessionStart` hooks written into every consumer project have **never fired** since June 2026. Context auto-flush and the HANDOFF.md snapshot have been inert in every install. The plugin's own `hooks/hooks.json` used the correct nested shape all along — the two files disagreed, and only the plugin-side one was valid.

**This started from a human report that "the plugin address is hardcoded to an old version and stops being found after an update."** Stale paths were real, but they were the symptom on top of a mechanism that had never worked. Four investigative steps got here: a developer discovering the self-heal already existed, a reviewer refusing to accept "it already works" without exercising it and finding the repair blind to the nested shape, an escalation I could not resolve read-only, and an authoritative docs answer. **No single step would have found it.**

## AC1 came first, and could have ended the ticket

I instructed the developer to verify my documentation-derived premise empirically **before building anything**, and to close the ticket as invalid if the flat shape turned out to be honoured. It ran `claude doctor` against real fixtures rather than trusting me, and the reviewer then reproduced that independently against **the actual emitted bytes** — including `Stop` with no `matcher` key — not merely "a nested shape."

The un-observed piece is narrow and disclosed: nested `claude -p` invocations are blocked by this sandbox's classifier, so nobody watched a hook physically fire. A hard schema rejection cannot have a code path to execution, and the TASK-209 reviewer independently observed the shipped 0.18.0 code repairing only `statusLine`. Adequate, and stated rather than glossed.

## The fix, and the half that matters most

The writer now emits nested. But a corrected writer only helps **new** projects — every existing one carries invalid entries on disk, and `--apply-settings` will not repair them (its presence checks match the *invalid* entry and skip the append; verified empirically).

So the substantive deliverable is `context-monitor/settings-migrate.mjs`: a new plugin-level `SessionStart` hook that migrates broken projects **automatically, with no user action and no release-notes reading**, mirroring `repin.mjs`'s established precedent. Heal-only, idempotent, leaves unrelated hooks and settings byte-identical.

**The two tickets compose deliberately:** TASK-209's `repin.mjs` owns *paths* across both shapes and never converts; this owns *shape* and never re-points an already-nested entry. Neither is sufficient alone. The reviewer could not construct an ordering where the two hooks' read-modify-write race leaves an entry half-migrated or stale — **convergence within ≤2 sessions, in both orderings.**

## Why it needed two fix rounds

**Round 1's race-guard sensor was vacuous.** It wrote the modified content *before* calling the function, so the guard never tripped and `skippedRace` was asserted nowhere. The entire mitigation for the concurrency hazard — on a hook that rewrites every consumer's settings file unattended — was an unspecced path guarded by a sensor that named it and did not exercise it. The spec's own comment conceded the limitation; **its title did not**, which is what made the gap invisible. Same failure mode TASK-207 hit.

**And the shipped skill still told developers to write the broken shape.** `skills/claude-code-context-monitor/SKILL.md` §7 prescribed the exact flat block `claude doctor` rejects — in a file that ships to consumers and is the authoritative reference for this subsystem. Fixing the generator while leaving the manual instructing people to break it is not a complete fix.

**The doc-lock built to close that found a second defect immediately:** the doc's command strings were missing the `node "<path>"` quoting the real writer always applies — wrong since TASK-008, and neither reviewer nor developer had caught it by reading. **Second time today a new sensor paid for itself on its first run.**

## The Empty-result finding, in the ticket labelled silent-failure

`migrateSettingsFile` originally returned a byte-identical value from **four distinct outcomes** — including **write failure** (EPERM, read-only `.claude`, disk full) indistinguishable from "nothing needed doing." The defect went six weeks unnoticed precisely because it failed silently, and the migration shipped with the same property.

Now a six-way `outcome` discriminant, with `main()` warning only on `malformed` and `write-failed` — the two that are genuinely not fine — and staying quiet on the three self-healing ones **by explicit decision, asserted, not by omission**. Always exits 0; never blocks a session.

`write-failed` was the last uncovered branch, and unforceable on Windows. The final round closed **both halves** via an injectable `writeSettings` seam mirroring the read seam — the message, and the real return path driven by a throwing writer with the on-disk file confirmed untouched. Leaving the failure-visibility branch as the one untested path would have been the wrong asymmetry to ship.

## Also closed

The superseded TASK-209 AC4 rationale in `src/claude-settings.js` — which its own commit disproved — now points at `repin.mjs`'s restated version. `collectFormatViolations` was extracted to a shared helper: **one schema, one validator, four consumers.** The e2e spec switched to a static import, closing a `test:changed` blind spot on an auto-running mutation path.

**Deferred, agreed on the merits:** first-match-only migration (unreachable through our own writer) and filename-substring ownership (only ever replaces a flat entry, which is already non-firing, so nothing working can be destroyed).
